title: Holes of the Compound run A2-2

definitions.guarantee: One locked requirement theorem of the task (task.json, spec/<lib>/Challenge.lean). Its statement in plain language is the doc comment of the property it asserts in the locked specification, quoted with line breaks joined by spaces; `readme` is the row of the task README's requirement table that names it, when there is one.
definitions.shape: The set of declarations the guarantee uses, directly or through others, following the constants the Lean kernel records in each declaration's type and value (the rule of the home page graph, under `rule`). The guarantee itself is not counted.
definitions.size: The number of declarations in the shape.
definitions.depth: The longest chain of uses from the guarantee down to a declaration that uses no other node: 0 for a declaration that uses none, else one more than its deepest dependency.
definitions.width: width[d] is the number of declarations of the shape whose own depth is d, for d from 0 to depth - 1.
definitions.loadBearing: `every`: the declarations in the shape of every guarantee of the task. `lemmas`: each lemma (a theorem that is not a requirement) in any shape, with the number of guarantees whose shape contains it.
definitions.hole: A declaration whose type or value contains `sorryAx`, as the Lean kernel records it (an explicit `sorry`: `sorry`; one Lean inserted for an elaboration error: `error`), including a required theorem left `sorry`. Only declarations in some shape are seen this way; a `sorry` in a declaration of the candidate that no guarantee reaches is listed under build.sorryOutsideShapes, from Lean's `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings, and no guarantee hangs from it.
definitions.hangsFrom: The holes in a guarantee's shape, or the guarantee itself when it is a hole. A guarantee hangs from those holes.
definitions.complete: A guarantee with no hole in its shape, that is not a hole itself, in a candidate that builds without errors.

rule: Nodes are the declarations reached from the requirement theorems by following the constants each declaration's type and value use, as the Lean kernel sees them, restricted to the candidate (final.lean) and the locked specification. Compiler-generated declarations are walked through, so their uses count for the declaration that generated them; constructors, recursors and projections count as their type; Lean's core library and ProofForgeFin are not shown (the ProofForgeFin declarations a node mentions are listed under its `library`). A declaration of the candidate that no requirement uses is left out and listed under excluded. An edge [a, b] means a uses b.

lean.runner: local release build of the toolchain (PF_LEAN_HOME)

statement.text: in a consistent state, every call succeeds: the policy hooks for any account, claims and speed changes never revert.

readme.text: in a consistent state (no side's block ahead of the current block, no recorded index above the market's), every call succeeds

statement.text: a supply hook brings the supply index up to date and credits `who` for exactly the supply rewards since its start (`accrualStart`), rounded down; nothing else changes.

readme.text: the full next state: the index brought up to date (`blocks * speed * 1e36 / total`, rounded down), the account credited `units * (index - start) / 1e36`, rounded down, from its start (`accrualStart`: its recorded index; with none recorded, `compInitialIndex` once the index has reached it, else 0), its index recorded, nothing else changed

statement.text: a borrow hook brings the borrow index up to date and credits `who` for exactly the borrow rewards since its start, rounded down; nothing else changes.

readme.text: the full next state: the index brought up to date (`blocks * speed * 1e36 / total`, rounded down), the account credited `units * (index - start) / 1e36`, rounded down, from its start (`accrualStart`: its recorded index; with none recorded, `compInitialIndex` once the index has reached it, else 0), its index recorded, nothing else changed

statement.text: a claim credits `who` on both sides as the hooks do and then pays it everything it has accrued when the Comptroller holds enough COMP.

readme.text: borrow side, then supply side, then payment of everything accrued when the Comptroller holds that much

statement.text: a speed change accrues what was emitted at the old speed and then applies the new speeds.

readme.text: a changed speed first accrues at the old speed

statement.text: from the upgrade of any well-formed pre-upgrade state, after any sequence of operations, the COMP paid out to accounts plus the COMP accrued to them never exceeds what they held or had accrued before the upgrade, plus what they were owed at the upgrade, plus the COMP emitted since.

the same for every single account: from the upgrade of any well-formed pre-upgrade state, no account ever holds or has accrued more COMP than it held or had accrued before the upgrade, plus what it was owed at the upgrade, plus the COMP emitted since.

readme.text: the same bound for every single account

statement.text: an account is never credited for blocks before it held a position. In any state reached from the upgrade of a well-formed pre-upgrade state, if an account holds no position, then whatever happens next it gains at most the COMP emitted from then on.

readme.text: an account with no position gains at most the COMP emitted from then on
